get.description: Get the status of currently running bots under your API key.
Get a single recording and its media files. 404 if the id is not one of your recordings.

Wait until someone in a live meeting addresses Claude by name, then return those lines.

Follow a live call without polling: call it in a loop, passing `next_index` back as
`since_index`, and speak only when `signal` is `addressed`. It blocks up to `timeout_sec`
and answers with ONE of: `addressed` — `lines` holds only the new lines that say "Claude"
(or «Клод») as a word; `quiet` — nothing addressed Claude, `new_lines` counts what was said;
`ended` — the meeting is over (any addressed lines in the last stretch included). With
`notes`, also `noted` — `noted` holds the new lines worth keeping on the meeting page, each
with its `kinds` (decision, commitment, price, date, new); at most one such answer a minute,
the lines in between batched into it. Read the whole transcript with get_meeting_transcript
when you need the context.

parameters.description: The first segment index not yet seen: 0 to start, then the `next_index` of the previous answer.

post.description:
Open the voice-note recorder in the person's Minutes tab, so they can dictate a note
that is transcribed like a meeting. You cannot record or hear audio yourself: this only
asks the person's open Minutes tab to start the recorder, and they speak and press Stop.
Call it when the person asks to record, dictate or take a voice note. It is refused in a
run with nobody present (a routine or background flow). Afterwards the note is a meeting
with platform voice_note: find it with list_meetings and read it with
get_meeting_transcript.
